question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(3\,\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(2x)) \\  & =3\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(2x)) \\  & =3\cdot (-\frac{1}{|2x|\sqrt{1+(2x)^{2}}})\cdot (2x)^{′} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2|x|\sqrt{1+4{x}^{2}}}\cdot 2 \\  & =-\frac{1}{|x|}\,\frac{3}{\sqrt{1+4{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
